t: Songtsen Gampo made Rasa, later called Lhasa, the capital of the Tibetan Empire in the 7th century and built the Jokhang and Ramoche temples there in 641 to house two Buddha statues.

After the empire fell in the 9th century political power lay elsewhere, but Lhasa became the centre of the Gelugpa school in the 15th century and the capital of the 5th Dalai Lama's government from 1642.
The Qing entered the city in 1720, a British expedition occupied it in 1904, and after 1950 and the flight of the 14th Dalai Lama in 1959 it became the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region in 1965.
dyk: Ancient Tibetan documents call the place Rasa, meaning "goat's place", a herding site. It was renamed Lhasa, "place of gods", when it became the capital and the Jokhang was completed to house a holy statue of the Buddha.
ev: Songtsen Gampo moves the capital to Rasa and raises the first structures on the site of the Potala
The Jokhang and Ramoche temples are built to house two Buddha statues
The 5th Dalai Lama moves the centre of his administration to Lhasa with the help of Güshi Khan
Reconstruction of the Potala Palace begins on Red Hill
The armies of the Qing dynasty enter Lhasa
A British expedition under Francis Younghusband captures and briefly occupies the city
The 14th Dalai Lama and his associates flee Tibet after a failed uprising
The Tibet Autonomous Region is established and Lhasa becomes its capital

f.founded: Songtsen Gampo moved the capital of the Tibetan Empire to Rasa (Lhasa) and in 637 raised the first structures on the site of the present Potala Palace; he built the Jokhang and Ramoche temples in 641.
f.where: On the middle reaches of the Lhasa (Kyi) River, a tributary of the Yarlung Zangbo (Brahmaputra), at about 3,650 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
f.known: The Jokhang and Ramoche temples; the Potala Palace; the seat of the Dalai Lamas; the Gelugpa monasteries of Ganden, Sera and Drepung; the Barkhor market and the pilgrim paths around it; Norbulingka; the British expedition of 1904
f.today: Lhasa is the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region, and the name is also used for the inner urban district of Lhasa City, Chengguan District.
